newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong to send home 1,200 Chinese children.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong to send home 1,200 Chinese children.

text.p: Hong Kong will repatriate more than 1,200 children who have been caught illegally entering the territory from China, an immigration official said on Thursday.
Immigration officer Leung Ping-kwan told reporters the children had been caught in the first quarter of this year, a big increase over the same period last year.
He blamed the influx on rumours spreading in China of an amnesty for children. Leung stressed there would be no amnesty and all illegal immigrant children would be sent back.
"If they realise that there is no amnesty, (and that) every illegal immigrant will be repatriated, I don't think they will risk their lives to come to Hong Kong illegally," he said.

Newspaper reports last month said Chinese parents now living legally in Hong Kong were paying up to HK$3,000 (US$390) to have their childrem who do not have Hong kong residency rights smuggled into the territory.
Chung Man-kwan, the Hong Kong father of an eight-year-old girl who entered the territory from China illegally, pleaded for mercy on Thursday.
"I beg the Governor and the immigration director to consider letting her stay on grounds of compassion and human rights, so that she can continue her schooling," he told reporters.

Leung noted about 35,000 Chinese children will have the right of abode in the territory after the British colony reverts to China on July 1 because of provisions in the post-colonial constitution, called the Basic Law.
But whether children who cross the border illegally can stay after the handover will be up to the future government, Leung said.
Hong Kong ends more than 150 years of British colonial rule and reverts to Chinese control.
